title.zh: 卷327 列傳一百十四 刘藻 杨应琚 杨重英 苏尔相 明瑞
title.en: Volume 327 Biographies 114: Liu Zao, Yang Yingju, Yang Zhongying, Su Erxiang, Ming Rui
title.raw: 卷327 列傳一百十四 刘藻 杨应琚 杨重英 苏尔相 明瑞

sentences.zh: =劉藻=劉藻，字素存，山東菏澤人。

translations.literal: =Liu Zao= Liu Zao, styled Sucun, was a native of Heze in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zao, whose courtesy name was Sucun, came from Heze in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 初名玉麟，以舉人授觀城教諭，乾隆元年，薦舉博學鴻詞，試一等，授檢討，更名。

translations.literal: His original name was Yulin. As a provincial graduate he was appointed instructor of Guancheng. In the first year of Qianlong he was recommended for the Boxue Hongci examination, placed in the first class, appointed revising compiler, and changed his name.
translations.idiomatic: He was first named Yulin. After passing the provincial examination he became instructor at Guancheng. In Qianlong year 1 (1736) he was nominated for the special erudition examination, ranked in the top tier, and was appointed a revising compiler in the Hanlin Academy, at which time he changed his name.

sentences.zh: 累遷左僉都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to the post of Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 圓明園工興，疏言：「園工不過少加補葺，視前代飾臺榭之觀者度越何啻萬萬？

translations.literal: When work began on the Old Summer Palace, he memorialized: "The garden work amounts to no more than minor repairs and patching. Compared with those of earlier dynasties who adorned terraces and towers, how is the difference not exceeded by tens of thousands of times?
translations.idiomatic: When construction at the Old Summer Palace was underway, he submitted a memorial: "The work on the gardens is merely modest patching and repair. Compared with past dynasties that lavished ornament on terraces and pavilions, the gap is surely not less than ten thousandfold.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為奢靡之漸，不可稍開。

translations.literal: Your subject humbly considers that the first steps toward extravagance must not be opened even slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is convinced that even the slightest opening toward extravagance must be resisted.

sentences.zh: 乞皇上慎始慮終，為天地惜物力，為國家培元氣，來歲諸工酌量停減。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to be cautious at the beginning and thoughtful to the end, to spare the material resources of Heaven and Earth, to nurture the vital energy of the state, and next year to reduce and suspend various projects as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to weigh the beginning against the end, conserve the resources of heaven and earth, restore the nation's vital strength, and next year scale back or halt these projects wherever prudence allows.

sentences.zh: 」上嘉納。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his advice with praise.

sentences.zh: 遷通政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Court of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Court of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 六年，擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: He supervised the educational administration of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Jiangsu education intendant.

sentences.zh: 尋以高郵諸生求賑而閧，左授宗人府府丞。

translations.literal: Soon, because students at Gaoyou rioted while seeking disaster relief, he was demoted one rank to Assistant Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, after Gaoyou students rioted while petitioning for famine relief, he was demoted to Assistant Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 藻居揚州候代，有吳之黼者，以文求教，藻行，饋糟魚，受之，中途發視，得白金四百，藻畀兩淮運使硃續晫還之黼。

translations.literal: When Zao was living in Yangzhou awaiting his replacement, a certain Wu Zhifu sought instruction in composition from him. When Zao departed, Wu presented fermented fish; he accepted it. En route he opened it and found four hundred taels of silver. Zao entrusted them to Zhu Xuzhuo, Transport Commissioner of the Two Huai, to return to Wu Zhifu.
translations.idiomatic: While waiting in Yangzhou to be relieved of his post, Zao was approached by Wu Zhifu, who sought literary instruction. When Zao left, Wu gave him a gift of fermented fish, which he accepted. On the road he discovered four hundred taels of silver hidden inside and handed them to Zhu Xuzhuo, the Two Huai transport commissioner, to return to Wu.

sentences.zh: 上聞，諭曰：「如此方不愧四知！

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he instructed: "Only in this way is he not unworthy of the Four Knows!
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, the emperor said, "Only conduct like this is worthy of the Four Knows!"

sentences.zh: 」旋乞養歸。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward he requested leave to retire and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon petitioned to retire and care for his parents at home.

sentences.zh: 孝賢皇后及長皇子定安親王喪，藻詣闕入見。

translations.literal: When Empress Xiaoxian and the eldest imperial son, Prince Ding'an, died, Zao went to the court to be received in audience.
translations.idiomatic: On the deaths of Empress Xiaoxian and the eldest prince, Prince Ding'an, Zao came to court for an audience.

sentences.zh: 會大學士張廷玉乞歸失上指，因獎藻，謂其知君臣休戚相關大義，以媿廷玉，加藻內閣學士銜，賜人葠二斤，命歸養母。

translations.literal: It happened that Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu's request to retire missed the emperor's intent. Thereupon the emperor praised Zao, saying he understood the great principle that ruler and minister share weal and woe, to shame Zhang Tingyu. He added to Zao the title of Grand Secretary of the Inner Court, bestowed two jin of ginseng, and ordered him home to care for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu's request to retire had displeased the emperor, who praised Zao instead for grasping that ruler and minister rise and fall together, pointedly to shame Zhang. He granted Zao the nominal rank of Inner Court grand secretary, gave him two jin of ginseng, and sent him home to nurse his mother.

sentences.zh: 母喪終，二十一年，授陝西布政使。

translations.literal: When his mother's mourning ended, in the twenty-first year he was appointed Financial Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's mourning period ended, in year 21 he was appointed financial commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，擢雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to Governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 he was promoted to governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 加太子少保，兼領貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and concurrently governed Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He received the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and concurrently served as governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，例行大計，巡撫圖爾炳阿未至，藻疏請先期舉行，上嘉之，旋授雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, at the regular triennial evaluation, Governor Tuerbing'a had not yet arrived. Zao memorialized to hold it in advance; the emperor commended this, and soon appointed him Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29, at the regular triennial personnel evaluation, Governor Tuerbing'a had not yet arrived. Zao memorialized to hold the review early; the emperor commended him and soon appointed him governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 三十年，疏言：「年來木梳野匪與緬甸所屬木邦構釁，又與耿馬土司毗連。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he memorialized: "In recent years Muzhu wild bandits have picked quarrels with Mobang under Burma, and they also adjoin the Gengma tusi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 30 he memorialized: "In recent years Muzhu bandits have clashed with Mobang, a dependency of Burma, and their territory also borders the Gengma chieftaincy."

sentences.zh: 自木邦至滾弄江，應設卡防守，請於各土司就近派撥。

translations.literal: From Mobang to the Gunong River, barrier posts should be set for defense; he requested that each tusi assign men nearby as needed.
translations.idiomatic: From Mobang to the Gunong River, barrier posts ought to be established for defense; he asked that each local chieftain assign troops from nearby districts.

sentences.zh: 」詔如所請。

translations.literal: " An edict approved as requested.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved his request.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，移湖廣總督，未行，尋奏：「副將趙宏榜等赴孟連、耿馬剿逐莽匪，鎮臣烏爾登額赴滾弄江口。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was transferred to Governor-General of Huguang but had not yet departed when he soon memorialized: "Vice Commander Zhao Hongbang and others went to Menglian and Gengma to pursue and expel Mang bandits; the regional commander Wuerdeng'e went to the mouth of the Gunong River.
translations.idiomatic: In year 31 he was transferred to governor-general of Huguang but had not yet left when he memorialized: "Vice Commander Zhao Hongbang and others have gone to Menglian and Gengma to drive out Mang bandits, and Regional Commander Wuerdeng'e has gone to the mouth of the Gunong River."

sentences.zh: 臣於普洱、思茅各隘調度。

translations.literal: Your subject is directing operations at the passes of Pu'er and Simao.
translations.idiomatic: I am coordinating operations at the passes of Pu'er and Simao.

sentences.zh: 」又奏言：「由小猛崙進攻九龍江、橄欖壩諸寨，多斬獲。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "Advancing from Xiaomenglun to attack the stockades of Jiulongjiang, Ganlanba, and others, many were killed and captured.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported: "Advancing from Xiaomenglun against the stockades at Jiulongjiang, Ganlanba, and elsewhere, our forces killed and captured many of the enemy."

sentences.zh: 惟參將何瓊詔、游擊明浩派赴整控江防禦，冒昧渡江，遇賊敗沒。

translations.literal: Only Regimental Commander He Qiong'zhao and Regional Commander Ming Hao, sent to defend on the Zhengkong River, rashly crossed the river, met the enemy, were defeated and lost.
translations.idiomatic: Regimental Commander He Qiong'zhao and Regional Commander Ming Hao, however, who had been sent to defend the Zhengkong River, rashly crossed the river, met the enemy, and were defeated with heavy losses."

sentences.zh: 」尋奏瓊詔等未死，請治貪功輕進之罪，上以「瓊詔、明浩等遇賊敗逃，又復妄言敗沒。

translations.literal: " Soon he memorialized that Qiong'zhao and others had not died and asked punishment for greedy advance; the emperor said: "Qiong'zhao, Ming Hao and others fled after defeat, yet falsely reported death in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported that Qiong'zhao and the others were not dead and asked that they be punished for reckless eagerness for merit. The emperor said, "Qiong'zhao, Ming Hao, and the rest fled after defeat and then falsely claimed they had been killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 此法所難宥，藻反稱冒昧貪功輕進，何憒憒乃爾」？

translations.literal: This offense the law can hardly pardon; yet Zao instead speaks of rash greedy light advance—how muddled can he be?"
translations.idiomatic: Such conduct the law can scarcely forgive, yet Zao calls it merely rash greed for glory—how muddled can he be?"

sentences.zh: 詔言：「藻本書生，軍行機宜，非其所習，朕不責以所不能。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Zao is fundamentally a scholar; military circumstances are not what he has practiced. I do not blame him for what he cannot do.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "Zao is fundamentally a scholar; the conduct of campaigns is not his training, and I do not hold him accountable for what he cannot do.

sentences.zh: 至調度賞罰，並可力為籌辦，乃舛謬若此，豈堪复勝總督之任？

translations.literal: But in deployment, rewards and punishments—all of these he could have exerted himself to arrange—yet he is so wildly wrong. How can he again bear the governorship?
translations.idiomatic: Yet in deployment and in rewards and punishments he could have applied himself fully; instead he has erred so gravely—how can he again be fit for a governor-general's post?

sentences.zh: 」因左授湖北巡撫，命楊應琚往代。

translations.literal: " Therefore he was demoted one rank to Governor of Hubei, and Yang Yingju was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore demoted to governor of Hubei, and Yang Yingju was ordered to take his place.

sentences.zh: 复諭：「應琚未至，藻當實力經理。

translations.literal: He again instructed: "Before Yingju arrives, Zao must manage affairs in earnest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor further instructed: "Until Yingju arrives, Zao must manage affairs with full diligence.

sentences.zh: 若自以為五日京兆，致誤事機，必重治其罪！

translations.literal: If he thinks himself a five-day capital magistrate and thereby misses the opportunity, his punishment will certainly be severe!"
translations.idiomatic: If he treats his post like a five-day magistracy and thereby misses the moment, he will be punished severely."

sentences.zh: 」部議奪職，留雲南效力。

translations.literal: " The ministry deliberation stripped his office but left him in Yunnan to serve.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry recommended stripping his rank while keeping him in Yunnan to serve.

sentences.zh: 藻聞上怒，惶迫自殺，巡撫常鈞疏報。

translations.literal: When Zao heard of the emperor's anger, in panic he killed himself; Governor Chang Jun reported by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When Zao learned of the emperor's anger, he killed himself in panic; Governor Chang Jun reported this by memorial.

sentences.zh: 上令應琚至普洱，為求醫治療，傷平，傳旨逮問。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yingju to Pu'er to seek medical treatment; when the wound healed, he transmitted an edict for arrest and interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yingju to Pu'er to have him treated; once the wound healed, an edict was sent for his arrest and interrogation.

sentences.zh: 常鈞旋奏藻死，上复詔責其張皇畏葸，旅襯歸葬，不得聽其家立碑書歷官事實。

translations.literal: Chang Jun soon memorialized that Zao had died. The emperor again edicted blaming his alarm and timidity; his coffin was sent home for burial and his family was not permitted to erect a stele recording his official career.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Jun soon reported that Zao had died. The emperor again rebuked his panic and timidity, ordered his body sent home for burial, and forbade his family from erecting a stele listing his official career.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，巡撫鄂寧奏言：「緬甸本莽瑞體之後。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, Governor E'ning memorialized: "Burma is originally descended from Mang Ruiti.
translations.idiomatic: In year 32, Governor E'ning memorialized: "Burma is originally the line of Mang Ruiti.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十八年，木梳頭目甕籍牙逐其酋莽打喇而自立。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Qianlong, the Muzhu chieftain Wengjiya drove out his ruler Mangdala and established himself.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong year 18 (1753), the Muzhu chieftain Wengjiya expelled his chief Mangdala and set himself up as ruler.

sentences.zh: 夷人遂呼緬甸為木梳，或呼緬，或呼莽，非二種也。

translations.literal: The barbarians then called Burma Muzhu, or called it Mian, or called it Mang—they are not two kinds.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen then called Burma Muzhu, or Mian, or Mang—these were not two separate peoples.

sentences.zh: =楊應琚=楊應琚，字佩之，漢軍正白旗人，廣東巡撫文乾子。

translations.literal: =Yang Yingju= Yang Yingju, styled Peizhi, was a Bannerman of the Plain White Han Army; he was the son of Wen Qian, Governor of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yingju, whose courtesy name was Peizhi, was a Plain White Banner Han Chinese; he was the son of Wen Qian, former governor of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 應琚起家任子。

translations.literal: Yingju began his career as the son of an official.
translations.idiomatic: Yingju entered official life through his father's privilege as a former official's son.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，自員外郎出為河東道，調西寧道。

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong, from department director he went out as Intendant of Hedong Circuit, then was transferred to Xining Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign he left the post of department director to become intendant of Hedong Circuit and was later transferred to Xining Circuit.

sentences.zh: 巡撫黃廷桂薦其才，高宗曰：「若能進於誠而擴充之，正未可量也。

translations.literal: Governor Huang Tinggui recommended his talent. The Gaozong Emperor said: "If he can advance in sincerity and expand upon it, his future truly cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Huang Tinggui recommended his ability. The Gaozong Emperor said, "If he can grow in sincerity and build on it, his prospects truly cannot be foretold."

sentences.zh: 」累遷至兩廣總督。

translations.literal: " He was promoted in succession to Governor-General of Guangdong and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 先後疏請練水師，籌軍食，修漓水、陡河堤壩，貯柳、桂、慶、梧餘鹽，皆如所請行。

translations.literal: In succession he memorialized to train the navy, provision military grain, repair the dikes and dams of the Li and Dou Rivers, and store surplus salt of Liu, Gui, Qing, and Wu—all were carried out as requested.
translations.idiomatic: He successively memorialized to train the navy, stock military provisions, repair the Li and Dou River dikes, and store surplus salt from Liu, Gui, Qing, and Wu; all were approved and implemented.

sentences.zh: 暹羅貢使毆傷通事，其國王鞫實，擬罰鍰，遣使牒禮部。

translations.literal: A Siamese tribute envoy beat and injured an interpreter; the Siamese king investigated the facts, proposed a fine, and sent an envoy with a note to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: A Siamese tribute envoy assaulted an interpreter; the Siamese king investigated, proposed a fine, and sent an envoy with a dispatch to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 應琚曰：「屬國陪臣無上交。

translations.literal: Yingju said: "Vassal states' attendant ministers have no dealings with the central government.
translations.idiomatic: Yingju said, "A vassal state's attendant ministers have no direct dealings with the central government."

sentences.zh: 」好語諭遣之，稱旨。

translations.literal: " He sent them away with kind words of instruction, which accorded with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed them with courteous instructions, which pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，移閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 he was transferred to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was given the additional title of Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 he received the additional title Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，移陝甘總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 he was transferred to governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 疏言伊犁底定，宜先屯田，留兵五千墾特諾果爾、長吉、羅克倫。

translations.literal: He memorialized that with Yili settled, colonization should come first; five thousand troops should be left to open fields at Tenoguo'er, Changji, and Luokelun.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that with Yili pacified, colonization should come first: five thousand troops should remain to farm Tenoguo'er, Changji, and Luokelun.

sentences.zh: 復以陝、甘非一督能治，請更西安總督為川陝總督，四川總督為巡撫，甘肅巡撫為總督，上遂命應琚督甘肅，陝西提鎮受節制，進太子太師。

translations.literal: He further argued that Shaanxi and Gansu could not be governed by one governor-general, and requested changing the Xi'an governor-general to Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general, the Sichuan governor-general to governor, and the Gansu governor to governor-general. The emperor then ordered Yingju to govern Gansu, with Shaanxi's provincial commander and regional commander under his command, and promoted him to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Shaanxi and Gansu were too much for one governor-general, and proposed renaming the Xi'an post Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general, demoting the Sichuan governor-general to provincial governor, and promoting the Gansu governor to governor-general. The emperor then put Yingju in charge of Gansu with Shaanxi's commanders under him and promoted him to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 嘗募巴爾楚克回戶治多蘭溝渠，墾喀喇沙爾以西各台，又增置兵備道、總兵，分駐阿克蘇、葉爾羌二城，逐為重鎮。

translations.literal: He once recruited Balkchugh Hui households to manage the Duolan canal, opened fields at the various stations west of Karashahr, and further added a military preparedness circuit intendant and regional commanders stationed separately at Aksu and Yarkand, which gradually became key strongholds.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited Balkchugh Muslim households to work the Duolan canal, opened farmland at the stations west of Karashahr, and added a military preparedness intendant and regional commanders garrisoned at Aksu and Yarkand, which gradually became major strongpoints.

sentences.zh: 應琚奏辦屯墾，遣兵購畜，部署紛煩；

translations.literal: Yingju memorialized on organizing colonization, sent troops to purchase livestock, and his deployments were tangled and burdensome;
translations.idiomatic: Yingju reported on organizing colonization, sent troops to buy livestock, and his arrangements grew tangled and burdensome;

sentences.zh: 至是，疏自言其非，請因利乘便規久遠。

translations.literal: At this point he memorialized acknowledging his errors and asked to take advantage of circumstances for long-term planning.
translations.idiomatic: At that point he memorialized admitting his mistakes and asked to plan for the long term by adapting to local conditions.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納，下其疏示中外。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it, and circulated his memorial within and without the court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved it with praise and circulated his memorial throughout the government.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，移駐肅州，拜東閣大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he moved his headquarters to Suzhou and was appointed Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 he moved his headquarters to Suzhou and was appointed Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，緬甸大入邊，滇事棘。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year Burma made a major incursion into the border; affairs in Yunnan became critical.
translations.idiomatic: In year 31 Burma launched a major border invasion, and affairs in Yunnan grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 緬酋莽達拉自為木梳長所篡，擊敗貴家木邦，貴酋宮裹雁奔孟連。

translations.literal: The Burmese chief Mangdala was himself usurped by the Muzhu chief, defeated the Guizhou-family Mobang, and the Guizhou chief Gongliyan fled to Menglian.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese chief Mangdala had been overthrown by the Muzhu leader, who defeated the Gu family of Mobang; the Gu chief Gongliyan fled to Menglian.

sentences.zh: 時應琚子重穀為永昌知府，誘殺之，木酋亦走。

translations.literal: At the time Yingju's son Chonggu was Prefect of Yongchang; he lured and killed him, and the Mobang chief also fled.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yingju's son Chonggu was prefect of Yongchang; he lured Gongliyan and killed him, and the Mobang chief also fled.

sentences.zh: 緬益橫，入犯思茅。

translations.literal: Burma grew still more aggressive and invaded Simao.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese grew bolder still and invaded Simao.

sentences.zh: 上移應珺雲貴總督視師。

translations.literal: The court transferred Yingju to Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou to oversee the army.
translations.idiomatic: The court transferred Yang Yingju to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou to take command in the field.

sentences.zh: 應琚至楚雄，緬人漸退，師乘間收復。

translations.literal: When Yingju reached Chuxiong, the Burmese gradually withdrew and the army seized the interval to recover territory.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingju reached Chuxiong, the Burmese gradually withdrew, and the army took advantage of the lull to recover ground.

sentences.zh: 應琚往孟良、整賣正經界，集流亡，釐戶口，定賦稅，而令召丙、叭先俸分據之，請賞給三品指揮使。

translations.literal: Yingju went to Mengliang and Zhengmai to rectify the border, gathered refugees, sorted households, fixed taxes, and ordered Zhaobing and Baxianfeng to hold separate territories, requesting that they be rewarded with third-rank commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Yingju went to Mengliang and Zhengmai to fix the border, gathered refugees, sorted households, set taxes, and placed Zhaobing and Baxianfeng in charge of separate districts, asking that they be granted third-rank commanders.

sentences.zh: 上以為能，賜珍物，官其孫茂齡藍翎侍衛。

translations.literal: The emperor considered him capable, bestowed precious objects, and appointed his grandson Maoling a blue-lance imperial bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged him capable, gave him precious gifts, and appointed his grandson Maoling a blue-lance imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 又使人誘致孟密、孟養、蠻暮令獻地，實則地懸緬境，內附特空言。

translations.literal: He also sent men to induce Mengmi, Mengyang, and Manmu to offer territory; in fact the land hung within Burmese territory, and submission to the interior was mere empty talk.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent agents to induce Mengmi, Mengyang, and Manmu to offer territory, but in fact those lands lay within Burma's sphere, so their submission was empty talk.

sentences.zh: 諸將希應琚指，爭謂緬勢孤，易攻取。

translations.literal: The generals, hoping to match Yingju's intent, all said Burma was isolated and easy to attack and seize.
translations.idiomatic: The generals, eager to please Yingju, all insisted Burma was isolated and easy to conquer.

sentences.zh: 應琚初猶弗聽，曰：「吾官至一品，年逾七十，復何所求，而以貪功開邊釁乎？

translations.literal: At first Yingju would not listen, saying: "My rank has reached the first grade and I am over seventy—what more do I seek, that I should open a border quarrel out of greed for merit?
translations.idiomatic: At first Yingju would not listen. He said, "I have reached the first rank and am past seventy—what more could I want, that I should open a border war out of greed for glory?"

sentences.zh: 」副將趙宏榜慫恿之，遂下道、鎮、府、州合議，亦謂寇勢大，邊釁不可開，總兵烏爾登額阻尤力，應琚滋不懌。

translations.literal: " Vice Commander Zhao Hongbang urged him on, whereupon he convened joint deliberation of circuit, garrison, prefecture, and department officials; they too said the enemy's strength was great and a border quarrel must not be opened. Regional Commander Wuerdeng'e opposed most forcefully, and Yingju grew still more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commander Zhao Hongbang egged him on, so he convened officials of circuit, garrison, prefecture, and department levels; they too said the enemy was strong and a border war must not be started. Regional Commander Wuerdeng'e opposed most strongly, and Yingju grew still more displeased.

sentences.zh: 永昌知府陳大呂懼更初議，應琚乃往永昌受降，並為文檄緬，侈言水陸軍五十萬陳境上，不降即進討。

translations.literal: Yongchang Prefect Chen Dalü feared a return to the original plan. Yingju then went to Yongchang to accept surrender and also drafted a proclamation to Burma, extravagantly claiming five hundred thousand land and naval troops arrayed on the border, and that if they did not submit he would advance to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchang Prefect Chen Dalü feared a reversal of the earlier plan. Yingju then went to Yongchang to accept surrender and issued a proclamation to Burma boasting that five hundred thousand land and naval troops stood on the frontier and threatening attack if they did not submit.

sentences.zh: 緬遂大發兵溯金沙江而上。

translations.literal: Burma then mobilized a large force and advanced up the Jinsha River.
translations.idiomatic: Burma then mobilized a large army and advanced up the Jinsha River.

sentences.zh: 其時宏榜頓新街，卻走。

translations.literal: At that time Hongbang was stationed at Xinjie and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hongbang was holding Xinjie but fell back.

sentences.zh: 應琚聞警即遘疾，上命楊廷璋往代，遣侍衛福靈安攜御醫往診；

translations.literal: When Yingju heard the alarm he immediately fell ill. The emperor ordered Yang Tingzhang to replace him and sent Bodyguard Fuling'an with an imperial physician to examine him;
translations.idiomatic: When Yingju heard the alarm he immediately took ill. The emperor ordered Yang Tingzhang to replace him and sent Bodyguard Fuling'an with an imperial physician to treat him;

sentences.zh: 並諭其子江蘇按察使重英、寶慶知府重穀省視。

translations.literal: and instructed his sons—the Jiangsu surveillance commissioner Chongying and the Baqing prefect Chonggu—to go and visit him.
translations.idiomatic: and told his sons—Jiangsu surveillance commissioner Chongying and Baqing prefect Chonggu—to go and attend him.

sentences.zh: 比廷璋至而疾已愈，乃令諸軍進擊，總兵硃崙出鐵壁關，攻楞木，不克，寇勢益張。

translations.literal: By the time Tingzhang arrived his illness had already abated; he then ordered the armies to advance. Regional Commander Zhu Lun went out through Tiewuguan to attack Lengmu but could not take it, and the enemy's momentum grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Tingzhang arrived Yingju had already recovered; he ordered the armies forward. Regional Commander Zhu Lun marched out through Iron Wall Pass to attack Lengmu but failed, and the enemy grew bolder.

sentences.zh: 提督李時升告急，應琚不報。

translations.literal: Provincial Commander Li Shisheng reported an emergency; Yingju did not relay it.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Commander Li Shisheng sent urgent reports; Yingju did not forward them.

sentences.zh: 緬陽議款，遂以楞木大捷入告，而緬已漸入戶臘撒。

translations.literal: The Burmese feigned willingness to negotiate peace; he then reported a great victory at Lengmu, while Burma had already gradually entered Huluosa.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese pretended to discuss peace, so he reported a great victory at Lengmu even as Burmese forces were already pushing into Huluosa.

sentences.zh: 時總兵劉德成擁兵幹崖，飲酒高會，時升屢趣罔應。

translations.literal: At the time Regional Commander Liu Decheng held troops at Ganya and held drinking feasts; Shisheng repeatedly urged him but got no response.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Regional Commander Liu Decheng kept his troops at Ganya feasting and drinking; Shisheng urged him repeatedly but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 應琚遣緬寧通判富森持令箭督戰，德成始抵盞達。

translations.literal: Yingju sent Dianning Subprefect Fusen with an order baton to supervise the battle; only then did Decheng reach Zanda.
translations.idiomatic: Yingju sent Dianning subprefect Fusen with an order baton to press the fight; only then did Decheng reach Zanda.

sentences.zh: 緬懼擊其後，潛引去，應琚仍以捷聞。

translations.literal: The Burmese, fearing a strike from the rear, quietly withdrew; Yingju still reported a victory.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese, fearing an attack from the rear, quietly withdrew; Yingju still reported a victory.

sentences.zh: 緬甸復入猛卯，參將哈國興等引還，砲械多遺失，應琚又報捷；

translations.literal: Burma again entered Mengmao; Regimental Commander Ha Guoxing and others led the troops back, and much artillery was lost; Yingju again reported a victory;
translations.idiomatic: Burma invaded Mengmao again; Regimental Commander Ha Guoxing and others led the troops back with much artillery lost; Yingju again reported a victory;

sentences.zh: 並傳令硃崙兼剿撫，陰示以和蕆事，緬果累乞和。

translations.literal: and transmitted orders to Zhu Lun to combine suppression and pacification, secretly hinting that peace would conclude matters; Burma indeed repeatedly begged for peace.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Zhu Lun to combine fighting with pacification, secretly signaling that peace would end the affair; the Burmese repeatedly sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，奏言：「緬甸酋弟卜坑率聶渺遮乞款附，懇予蠻暮、新街互市。

translations.literal: After a year he memorialized: "The Burmese chief's younger brother Bokeng led Ni Miaozhe to beg to submit in peace and earnestly asked for mutual markets at Manmu and Xinjie.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he memorialized: "The Burmese chief's younger brother Bokeng led Ni Miaozhe to sue for peace and asked permission for trade at Manmu and Xinjie."

sentences.zh: 」上察其偽，數訶責。

translations.literal: " The emperor perceived the deception and repeatedly rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw through the deception and rebuked him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 嗣木邦告警，國興軍抵蠻暮，寇★K4退，應琚又以復新街奏。

translations.literal: Later Mobang raised an alarm; Guoxing's army reached Manmu and the bandits ★K4 retreated; Yingju again memorialized the recovery of Xinjie.
translations.idiomatic: Later Mobang sent an alarm; Guoxing's army reached Manmu and the enemy withdrew; Yingju again memorialized the recovery of Xinjie.

sentences.zh: 上視所進地圖，疑寇既屢敗，何以尚據內地土司境，降旨駁詰。

translations.literal: The emperor looked at the map submitted and doubted: if the bandits had been repeatedly defeated, why did they still hold territory within interior tusi domains? He issued an edict to refute and question this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor examined the map submitted and asked how, if the enemy had been beaten so often, they still held ground inside interior chieftaincies; he sent an edict demanding an explanation.

sentences.zh: 會福靈安先被命廉軍事，具言宏榜諸人失守狀，應琚亦劾德成等遲留不進，於是俱逮問，而以楊寧為提督，且以應琚不勝任，召明瑞代統其軍。

translations.literal: It happened that Fuling'an had already been ordered to investigate military affairs and detailed how Hongbang and others had lost their posts; Yingju also impeached Decheng and others for delay and failure to advance. Thereupon all were arrested for interrogation; Yang Ning was made provincial commander, and because Yingju was incompetent, Ming Rui was summoned to take command of his army.
translations.idiomatic: Fuling'an had already been ordered to investigate the campaign and reported how Hongbang and others had lost their positions; Yingju also impeached Decheng and others for stalling. All were then arrested; Yang Ning was made provincial commander, and because Yingju was unfit for command, Ming Rui was summoned to replace him.

sentences.zh: 明瑞至，首發其欺罔罪，謂誤木緬別為一事尤妄誕，鄂寧亦糾其掩敗為勝。

translations.literal: When Ming Rui arrived, he first exposed his crime of deception, saying that the error of treating Muzhu and Burma as separate matters was especially absurd; E'ning also impeached him for concealing defeat as victory.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming Rui arrived, he first exposed Yingju's deceit, saying that treating Muzhu and Burma as separate entities was especially absurd; E'ning also charged him with reporting defeats as victories.

sentences.zh: 應琚恐，乃上言大舉徵緬，調湖廣、川、滇軍五萬，五路並進，請敕暹羅夾攻，朝論皆斥之。

translations.literal: Yingju, in fear, then memorialized for a major campaign against Burma, mobilizing fifty thousand troops from Huguang, Sichuan, and Yunnan in five columns advancing together, and asked an edict for Siam to attack from both sides; court opinion all rejected this.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Yingju then proposed a major expedition against Burma: fifty thousand troops from Huguang, Sichuan, and Yunnan advancing in five columns, with Siam ordered to attack from the flank; the court unanimously rejected it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔逮問，賜死。

translations.literal: Before long an edict ordered his arrest and interrogation and granted him death.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered his arrest; he was granted death by suicide.

sentences.zh: 重穀亦坐笞殺人，棄市。

translations.literal: Chonggu was also punished for beating a man to death and was executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Chonggu was also convicted of beating a man to death and was executed in public.

sentences.zh: 重英初至雲南，隱以監軍自居，嗣為鄂寧所劾，命以知府從軍。

translations.literal: When Chongying first reached Yunnan he privately regarded himself as army supervisor; later he was impeached by E'ning and ordered to follow the army as a prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongying first reached Yunnan he quietly acted as if he were supervising the army; later E'ning impeached him, and he was ordered to serve with the army merely as a prefect.

sentences.zh: 明年，軍士患飢，緬嗛詐媾和，參贊珠魯訥遣重英往報，被執。

translations.literal: The next year the soldiers suffered hunger; the Burmese feigned willingness to negotiate peace; Coordinator Zhulune sent Chongying to reply and he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the troops were starving; the Burmese pretended to negotiate peace; Coordinator Zhulune sent Chongying to respond and he was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 上以重英且降緬，下其子長齡獄。

translations.literal: The emperor, thinking Chongying would soon surrender to Burma, imprisoned his son Changling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, believing Chongying would soon defect to Burma, imprisoned his son Changling.

sentences.zh: 已，緬歸俘卒，賚貝葉書，附重英書乞罷兵，拒弗納。

translations.literal: Later Burma returned captive soldiers and sent a palm-leaf letter, with a letter from Chongying attached begging to cease hostilities; this was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Later Burma returned captive soldiers with a palm-leaf letter and a note from Chongying begging to end the war; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，緬出都司蘇爾相議和，仍弗許。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year Burma sent out the battalion commander Su Erxiang to discuss peace; this was still not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In year 41 Burma sent Battalion Commander Su Erxiang to negotiate peace; the court still refused.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，緬聞暹羅受封，乃款關求貢，並還重英。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year, hearing that Siam had received investiture, Burma then presented itself at the border seeking tribute and also returned Chongying.
translations.idiomatic: In year 53, learning that Siam had received investiture, Burma came to the border to offer tribute and also returned Chongying.

sentences.zh: 重英陷緬後，獨居佛寺逾二十年，未改中國衣冠。

translations.literal: After Chongying was trapped in Burma, he lived alone in a Buddhist temple for more than twenty years without changing his Chinese dress.
translations.idiomatic: After he fell into Burmese hands, Chongying lived alone in a Buddhist temple for more than twenty years without abandoning Chinese dress.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，進道員，釋長齡出獄，比以蘇武之節，御製蘇楊論旌之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, promoted him to circuit intendant, released Changling from prison, compared him to Su Wu's steadfastness, and composed the Discourse on Su and Yang to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, promoted him to circuit intendant, freed Changling from prison, compared his conduct to Su Wu's loyalty, and composed an imperial essay, Discourse on Su and Yang, to honor him.

sentences.zh: 俄，病卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: =蘇爾相=蘇爾相，甘肅靈州人。

translations.literal: =Su Erxiang= Su Erxiang was a native of Lingzhou in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Su Erxiang came from Lingzhou in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 自行伍從征緬甸、金川有勞，累遷雲南奇兵營都司。

translations.literal: From the ranks he followed campaigns against Burma and Jinchuan with merit and was promoted in succession to Battalion Commander of the Yunnan Irregular Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Rising from the ranks, he served with distinction in the Burma and Jinchuan campaigns and was promoted to battalion commander of the Yunnan Irregular Battalion.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，雲貴總督彰寶以緬甸表貢久不至，遣爾相齎檄往諭，被留，迫使上書阿桂申表貢之議。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, Governor-General Zhangbao of Yunnan-Guizhou, because Burma's tribute memorial had long failed to arrive, sent Erxiang with a proclamation to instruct them; he was detained and forced to write to Agui urging the tribute proposal.
translations.idiomatic: In year 35, Governor-General Zhangbao of Yunnan-Guizhou, because Burma's tribute memorial had long been overdue, sent Erxiang with a proclamation to remonstrate with them; the Burmese detained him and forced him to write Agui urging tribute.

sentences.zh: 上謂爾相且降緬，命甘肅疆吏執爾相妻孥致京師，子一、女二死於獄，妻死於道。

translations.literal: The emperor thought Erxiang would soon surrender to Burma and ordered Gansu frontier officials to arrest his wife and children and send them to the capital; one son and two daughters died in prison, and the wife died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed Erxiang would soon defect to Burma and ordered Gansu officials to seize his family and send them to the capital; one son and two daughters died in prison, and his wife died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，緬始送爾相還。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year Burma at last sent Erxiang back.
translations.idiomatic: In year 41 Burma at last sent Erxiang home.

sentences.zh: 上命阿桂傳諭，令其詣京師，引見，授游擊，賜詩亦比以蘇武。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Agui to transmit instructions for him to proceed to the capital for an audience; he was appointed Regional Commander and given a poem also comparing him to Su Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Agui to instruct him to come to the capital for an audience; he was appointed regional commander and given an imperial poem comparing him to Su Wu.

sentences.zh: 累遷騰越鎮總兵，兼署雲南提督。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Regional Commander of Tengyue Garrison and concurrently acted as Yunnan Provincial Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to regional commander of Tengyue and concurrently served as acting provincial commander of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: =明瑞=明瑞，字筠亭，富察氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人，承恩公富文子。

translations.literal: =Ming Rui= Ming Rui, styled Yunting, of the Fuca clan, a Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Manchu Banner, son of Duke Fuwen of Eng'en.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Rui, whose courtesy name was Yunting, was of the Fuca clan, a Bordered Yellow Banner Manchu, and son of Duke Fuwen of Eng'en.

sentences.zh: 自官學生襲爵。

translations.literal: As a student of the Imperial School he inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the family title as a graduate of the Imperial School.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十一年，師徵阿睦爾撒納，明瑞以副都統銜授領隊大臣，有功，擢戶部侍郎，授參贊大臣，於公爵加「毅勇」字，號承恩毅勇公。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Qianlong, when the army campaigned against Amursana, Ming Rui with vice commander rank was appointed leading minister; for merit he was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and appointed coordinating minister; on his dukedom were added the characters Yi Yong, and he was titled Duke of Eng'en Yi Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong year 21, during the campaign against Amursana, Ming Rui served as leading minister with vice commander rank; for merit he became vice minister of revenue and coordinating minister, and his ducal title gained the epithet Yi Yong, making him Duke of Eng'en Yi Yong.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，師徵霍集占，復有功，賜雙眼花翎，加雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, when the army campaigned against Khoja Jahan, he again had merit, was granted double-eyed peacock feathers, and given the hereditary office of Cloud Cavalry Captain.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24, during the campaign against Khoja Jahan, he distinguished himself again and received double-eyed peacock feathers and a hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captain commission.

sentences.zh: 師還，圖形紫光閣，擢正白旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: When the army returned, his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor; he was promoted to Commander of the Plain White Han Army Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, his portrait was hung in the Hall of Purple Splendor and he was promoted to commander of the Plain White Han Army Banner.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，出為伊犁將軍，進加騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he went out as General of Yili and was further given the hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 he was appointed general of Yili and received an additional hereditary Cavalry Commandant commission.

sentences.zh: 三十年二月，烏什回為亂，駐烏什副都統素誠自戕，亂回推小伯克賴黑木圖拉為渠，拒守。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirtieth year the Ush Hui rebelled; the Ush garrison vice commander Sucheng killed himself; the rebels made the petty beg Laheimtula their leader and held out in defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 30 the Ush Muslims rebelled; Vice Commander Sucheng, stationed at Ush, killed himself; the rebels made the petty beg Laheimtula their leader and held the city.

sentences.zh: 明瑞遣副都統觀音保往討，而帥師繼其後。

translations.literal: Ming Rui sent Vice Commander Guanyinbao to attack while he himself led the army after him.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Rui sent Vice Commander Guanyinbao ahead to attack while he followed with the main army.

sentences.zh: 烏什回二千餘出禦，明瑞與觀音保力戰破之，奪砲台七。

translations.literal: More than two thousand Ush Hui came out to resist; Ming Rui and Guanyinbao fought fiercely and defeated them, capturing seven batteries.
translations.idiomatic: More than two thousand Ush rebels came out to fight; Ming Rui and Guanyinbao broke them in hard fighting and took seven batteries.

sentences.zh: 賊入城，師合圍。

translations.literal: The bandits entered the city and the army invested it on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels retreated into the city and the army surrounded it.

sentences.zh: 明瑞疏陳素誠狂縱激變，及參贊納世通虐回民，阻援師，副都統弁塔哈掩敗妄奏諸狀，上令尚書阿桂至軍，按誅納世通、弁塔哈。

translations.literal: Ming Rui memorialized that Sucheng's arrogance and license had provoked the uprising, that Coordinator Nashitong had abused the Hui people and blocked relief troops, and that Vice Commander Biantaha had concealed defeat and falsely reported; the emperor ordered Minister Agui to the army to investigate and execute Nashitong and Biantaha.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Rui reported that Sucheng's arrogance had provoked the revolt, that Coordinator Nashitong had abused the Muslims and blocked reinforcements, and that Vice Commander Biantaha had concealed defeats; the emperor sent Minister Agui to the army to try and execute Nashitong and Biantaha.

sentences.zh: 賊夜襲我軍，我軍诇知之，預為備，射賴黑木圖拉殪，賊擁其父額色木圖拉為渠。

translations.literal: The bandits raided our army by night; our army learned of it by reconnaissance and prepared in advance, shooting Laheimtula dead; the bandits made his father Eskimtula their leader.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels attacked by night, but scouts gave warning and the troops were ready; Laheimtula was shot dead, and the rebels raised his father Eskimtula as leader.

sentences.zh: 明瑞以兵六百餘夜攜雲梯薄其城，不克，則毀其堞，且斷汲道。

translations.literal: Ming Rui with more than six hundred troops at night carried scaling ladders close to the wall but could not take it; he then destroyed the parapets and cut off the water route.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Rui led more than six hundred men at night with scaling ladders against the wall but failed; he then destroyed the parapets and cut off the water supply.

sentences.zh: 賊待阿富汗援不至，乃縛獻額色木圖拉等四十二人降，明瑞悉斬之，其脅從及婦稚萬餘送伊犁。

translations.literal: The bandits, waiting for Afghan aid that did not come, then bound and presented Eskimtula and forty-two others to surrender; Ming Rui executed them all, and more than ten thousand followers, women, and children were sent to Yili.
translations.idiomatic: When Afghan aid failed to arrive, the rebels bound Eskimtula and forty-one others and surrendered; Ming Rui executed them all and sent more than ten thousand followers, women, and children to Yili.

sentences.zh: 烏什平。

translations.literal: Ush was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Ush was pacified.

sentences.zh: 上以明瑞得渠魁，未詳鞫為亂狀，亂回至圍急始縛獻首惡，不可輕宥，所措置皆不當，與阿桂同下部議，奪職，命留任。

translations.literal: The emperor held that though Ming Rui had obtained the ringleader, he had not thoroughly investigated the causes of the rebellion; the rebels had only bound and presented the chief culprit when the siege grew desperate and could not be lightly pardoned; all his dispositions were improper. He and Agui were both referred to the ministry for deliberation, stripped of office, and ordered to remain at their posts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that although Ming Rui had captured the ringleader, he had not fully investigated the rebellion; the rebels had surrendered their leaders only when desperate, which could not be lightly forgiven, and his arrangements were all wrong. He and Agui were referred to the ministry, stripped of rank, and ordered to remain on duty.

sentences.zh: 旋條上善後事，如所請。

translations.literal: Soon he submitted items on post-pacification measures, which were approved as requested.
translations.idiomatic: He soon submitted a plan for post-pacification measures, which was approved.

sentences.zh: 是時緬甸為亂犯邊，總督劉藻戰屢敗，自殺。

translations.literal: At this time Burma rebelled and invaded the border; Governor Liu Zao was repeatedly defeated in battle and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Burma raided the frontier; Governor Liu Zao suffered repeated defeats and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 大學士楊應琚代為總督，師久無功，賜死。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Yang Yingju replaced him as governor-general; the army long achieved no success and he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yang Yingju replaced him as governor-general; the campaign dragged on without success, and he was granted death.

sentences.zh: 三十二年二月，命明瑞以雲貴總督兼兵部尚書，經略軍務。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirty-second year Ming Rui was ordered to serve as Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou and concurrently Minister of War to oversee military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 32 Ming Rui was appointed governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou and concurrent minister of war to direct the campaign.

sentences.zh: 明瑞議大軍出永昌、騰越攻宛頂、木邦為正兵，遣參贊額爾登額出北路，自猛密攻老官屯，會於阿瓦。

translations.literal: Ming Rui proposed that the main army advance from Yongchang and Tengyue to attack Wanding and Mobang as the principal force, while Coordinator E'erdeng'e would go by the northern route from Mengmi to attack Laoguantun, meeting at Ava.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Rui planned the main army out of Yongchang and Tengyue against Wanding and Mobang, while Coordinator E'erdeng'e would take the northern route from Mengmi against Laoguantun to meet at Ava.

sentences.zh: 十一月，至宛頂，進攻木邦，賊遁，留參贊珠魯訥、按察使楊重英守之，率兵萬餘渡錫箔江攻蠻結。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he reached Wanding and advanced on Mobang; the bandits fled. He left Coordinator Zhulune and Surveillance Commissioner Yang Chongying to guard it, then led more than ten thousand troops across the Xibo River to attack Manjie.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he reached Wanding and attacked Mobang; the enemy fled. He left Coordinator Zhulune and Surveillance Commissioner Yang Chongying to hold it, then led more than ten thousand men across the Xibo River against Manjie.

sentences.zh: 寇二萬，立十六寨，寨外浚溝，溝外又環以木柵，列象陣為伏兵。

translations.literal: The enemy numbered twenty thousand, established sixteen stockades, dug ditches outside the stockades, and ringed the ditches with wooden palisades, arraying elephant formations as ambush troops.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty thousand enemy troops built sixteen stockades, dug ditches around them, ringed the ditches with wooden palisades, and posted elephant formations in ambush.

sentences.zh: 明瑞統兵居中，領隊大臣扎拉豐阿、李全據東山梁，觀音保、長青據西山梁。

translations.literal: Ming Rui commanded the center; Leading Ministers Zhalafeng'a and Li Quan held the eastern hill ridge; Guanyinbao and Changqing held the western hill ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Rui held the center; Leading Ministers Zhala Feng'a and Li Quan took the eastern ridge; Guanyinbao and Changqing took the western ridge.

sentences.zh: 賊突陣西出，觀音保、長青力戰，明瑞督中軍進，殺賊二百餘，賊退保柵。

translations.literal: The bandits burst out from the western wing of the formation; Guanyinbao and Changqing fought fiercely; Ming Rui directed the center army forward and killed more than two hundred bandits; the bandits retreated to hold the palisades.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy broke out on the west; Guanyinbao and Changqing fought hard while Ming Rui led the center forward, killing more than two hundred; the enemy fell back behind the palisades.

sentences.zh: 明瑞令分兵為十二隊，身先陷陣，目傷，猶指揮不少挫。

translations.literal: Ming Rui ordered the troops divided into twelve companies, took the lead in storming the formation, was wounded in the eye, yet continued to command without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Rui divided his force into twelve companies, led the charge himself, was wounded in the eye, yet kept commanding without faltering.

sentences.zh: 賊陣中群象反奔，我兵毀柵進，無不一當百。

translations.literal: The elephants in the enemy formation stampeded back; our troops destroyed the palisades and advanced, each fighting as if a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy elephants panicked and turned back; our troops smashed the palisades and advanced, each man fighting like a hundred.

sentences.zh: 有貴州兵王連者，舞藤牌躍入陣，眾從之，縱橫擊殺，馘二十餘，俘三十有四，賊遁走。

translations.literal: A Guizhou soldier named Wang Lian danced with a rattan shield and leaped into the formation; the masses followed, striking and killing in all directions, taking more than twenty heads and thirty-four captives; the bandits fled.
translations.idiomatic: A Guizhou soldier named Wang Lian vaulted into the enemy line with his rattan shield; others followed, cutting down the foe in every direction, taking more than twenty heads and thirty-four prisoners, and the enemy fled.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，上大悅，封一等誠嘉毅勇公，賜黃帶、寶石頂、四團龍補服，原襲承恩公畀其弟奎林。

translations.literal: When news of the victory arrived the emperor was greatly pleased, enfeoffed him as Duke of First Rank Cheng Jiayi Yong, bestowed the yellow belt, jeweled finial, and four-dragon roundel surcoat, and gave the original inherited dukedom of Eng'en to his younger brother Kuilin.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported the emperor was delighted, created him Duke of First Rank Cheng Jiayi Yong, gave him the yellow belt, jeweled finial, and four-dragon surcoat, and transferred the original Eng'en dukedom to his younger brother Kuilin.

sentences.zh: 扎拉豐阿、觀音保勸明瑞乘勝罷兵，明瑞不可。

translations.literal: Zhalafeng'a and Guanyinbao urged Ming Rui to cease operations on the momentum of victory; Ming Rui would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhala Feng'a and Guanyinbao urged Ming Rui to halt on the momentum of victory; he refused.

sentences.zh: 師復進，十二月，次革龍，地逼天生橋渡口，賊踞山巔立柵。

translations.literal: The army advanced again. In the twelfth month it halted at Gelong, where the ground pressed upon the Tian Sheng Bridge crossing; the bandits held the mountain summit and erected palisades.
translations.idiomatic: The army pushed on. In the twelfth month it reached Gelong, near the Tian Sheng Bridge crossing, where the enemy held the heights behind palisades.

sentences.zh: 明瑞令別軍出大道，若將奪渡口，而督軍從間道繞至天生橋上游，乘霧徑渡，進據山梁。

translations.literal: Ming Rui ordered a separate force out on the main road as if to seize the crossing, while he himself led the army by a bypath around to above Tian Sheng Bridge, crossed directly in the fog, and advanced to seize the hill ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Rui sent a detachment along the main road as if to seize the crossing, while he led the main force by a hidden path above Tian Sheng Bridge, crossed in the fog, and seized the ridge.

sentences.zh: 賊驚潰，浮馘二千餘。

translations.literal: The bandits fled in panic; more than two thousand bodies floated on the water.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy broke in panic; more than two thousand bodies floated on the water.

sentences.zh: 復進至象孔，糧垂罄，欲退，慮額爾登額師已入，聞猛籠土司糧富，且地近猛密，冀通北路軍消息，乃移軍猛籠。

translations.literal: He advanced again to Xiangkong; grain was nearly exhausted and he wished to retreat, but feared E'erdeng'e's army had already entered. Hearing that the Menglong tusi had rich grain and that the place was near Mengmi, hoping to establish contact with the northern-route army, he moved the army to Menglong.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Xiangkong, but supplies were almost gone and he considered retreating, yet feared E'erdeng'e's column had already entered. Hearing that the Menglong chieftain had abundant grain and lay near Mengmi, he hoped to link up with the northern force and moved to Menglong.

sentences.zh: 賊尾我軍後，至章子壩，我軍且戰且行。

translations.literal: The bandits followed behind our army to Zhangziba; our army fought as it marched.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy pursued to Zhangziba, and the army fought as it marched.

sentences.zh: 明瑞及觀音保等殿，日行不三十里，至猛籠已歲除，土司避匿，發窖粟二萬餘石。

translations.literal: Ming Rui and Guanyinbao and others brought up the rear, marching no more than thirty li a day. When they reached Menglong it was already New Year's Eve; the tusi had hidden away, but they uncovered more than twenty thousand shi of stored grain.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Rui, Guanyinbao, and others covered the retreat, making barely thirty li a day. They reached Menglong on New Year's Eve; the chieftain had fled, but they found more than twenty thousand shi of grain in storage.

sentences.zh: 駐三日，復引軍趨猛密，人持數升粟，焚其餘積。

translations.literal: After halting three days he again led the army toward Mengmi; each man carried a few sheng of grain and burned the rest of the stores.
translations.idiomatic: After three days' halt he marched toward Mengmi, each man carrying only a few sheng of grain while the rest was burned.

sentences.zh: 賊躡我軍行，至夕駐營，初相距十餘裡。

translations.literal: The bandits tracked our army's march; when we camped at evening they were at first more than ten li distant.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy shadowed the march; when the army camped at evening they were still more than ten li behind.

sentences.zh: 賊诇我軍飢疲，經蠻化，我軍屯山巔，賊即營山半。

translations.literal: The bandits learned by reconnaissance that our army was hungry and weary. Passing Manhua, our army camped on the mountain summit and the bandits immediately encamped halfway up the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts told the enemy the army was starving and exhausted. At Manhua our troops camped on the summit while the enemy camped halfway up the slope.

sentences.zh: 明瑞謂諸將曰：「賊輕我甚，不一死戰，無焦類矣！

translations.literal: Ming Rui said to the generals: "The bandits despise us greatly; if we do not fight to the death, not one of us will survive!
translations.idiomatic: Ming Rui told his generals, "The enemy despises us utterly; unless we fight to the death, none of us will survive!"

sentences.zh: 賊識我軍號。

translations.literal: The bandits recognize our army's signals.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy know our camp signals.

sentences.zh: 明旦我軍傳號，若將起行，則盡出營伏箐待。

translations.literal: At dawn let our army sound the signals as if about to depart; then all leave camp and lie in ambush in the ravines to wait.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn we will sound the march call as if breaking camp; then everyone will leave camp and lie in ambush in the ravines.

sentences.zh: 」明旦賊聞聲，蟻附上山。

translations.literal: " At dawn the bandits heard the sounds and swarmed up the mountain like ants.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the enemy heard the signals and swarmed up the mountain.

sentences.zh: 我軍突出發槍砲，賊反走，乘之，斬四千有奇。

translations.literal: Our army burst out and fired muskets and cannon; the bandits turned and fled; we pursued and cut down more than four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Our troops sprang from ambush with muskets and cannon; the enemy fled and were pursued; more than four thousand were killed.

sentences.zh: 自此每夜遙屯二十里外，明瑞令休兵六日。

translations.literal: From then on each night they camped far off twenty li away; Ming Rui ordered six days' rest for the troops.
translations.idiomatic: After that the enemy camped twenty li away each night, and Ming Rui gave the army six days' rest.

sentences.zh: 賊柵於要道，我軍攻之不能拔，得波霙人引自桂家銀廠舊址出。

translations.literal: The bandits palisaded the vital road; our army attacked but could not take it, until Bo'ying tribesmen guided them out by the old site of the Guijia silver mine.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy blocked the main road with palisades and could not be dislodged until Bo'ying guides led the army out by the old Guijia silver-mine route.

sentences.zh: 上聞明瑞深入，命全師速出。

translations.literal: The emperor, hearing that Ming Rui had penetrated deeply, ordered the entire army to withdraw quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Ming Rui had penetrated too far, the emperor ordered the whole army to withdraw at once.

sentences.zh: 詔未達，三十三年正月，賊攻木邦，副都統珠魯訥師潰自戕，執重英以去。

translations.literal: Before the edict arrived, in the first month of the thirty-third year the bandits attacked Mobang; Vice Commander Zhulune's army collapsed and he killed himself; they seized Chongying and took him away.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict arrived, in the first month of year 33 the enemy attacked Mobang; Vice Commander Zhulune's force collapsed and he killed himself, and the Burmese seized Chongying.

sentences.zh: 額爾登額出猛密，阻於老官屯，月餘引還。

translations.literal: E'erdeng'e came out of Mengmi but was blocked at Laoguantun; after more than a month he led his troops back.
translations.idiomatic: E'erdeng'e advanced from Mengmi but was blocked at Laoguantun and withdrew after more than a month.

sentences.zh: 繞從小隴川緩行，巡撫鄂寧檄援，不應，於是明瑞軍援絕，而賊自木邦、老官屯兩道並集。

translations.literal: He made a detour by way of Xiaolongchuan and marched slowly; Governor E'ning sent orders for aid but received no response. Thus Ming Rui's army was cut off from relief, while the bandits converged from Mobang and Laoguantun in two columns.
translations.idiomatic: He detoured by Xiaolongchuan and marched slowly; Governor E'ning called for help but got no response. Ming Rui's army was cut off, while the enemy converged from Mobang and Laoguantun in two columns.

sentences.zh: 二月，至小猛育，賊麕聚五萬餘。

translations.literal: In the second month they reached Xiaomengyu; the bandits gathered more than fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month they reached Xiaomengyu, where more than fifty thousand enemy troops had massed.

sentences.zh: 我軍食罄，殺馬騾以食；

translations.literal: Our army's food was exhausted and they killed horses and mules for food;
translations.idiomatic: Our troops ran out of food and slaughtered horses and mules to eat;

sentences.zh: 火藥亦竭，槍砲不能發。

translations.literal: Gunpowder was also exhausted and muskets and cannon could not be fired.
translations.idiomatic: Gunpowder ran out as well, and muskets and cannon could no longer be fired.

sentences.zh: 明瑞令諸將達興阿、本進忠分隊潰圍出，而自為殿，血戰萬寇中。

translations.literal: Ming Rui ordered the generals Da Xing'a and Ben Jinzhong to break out in separate columns while he himself brought up the rear, fighting in bloody combat amid tens of thousands of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Rui ordered Generals Da Xing'a and Ben Jinzhong to break out in separate columns while he covered the retreat, fighting hand to hand among tens of thousands of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 扎拉豐阿、觀音保皆死。

translations.literal: Zhalafeng'a and Guanyinbao both died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhala Feng'a and Guanyinbao were both killed.

sentences.zh: 明瑞負創行二十餘裡，手截辮髮授其僕歸報，而縊於樹下，其僕以木葉掩屍去。

translations.literal: Ming Rui, wounded, went more than twenty li, cut off his queue with his own hand and gave it to his servant to return and report, then hanged himself beneath a tree; his servant covered the corpse with leaves and left.
translations.idiomatic: Wounded, Ming Rui went more than twenty li, cut off his queue and gave it to a servant to carry back word, then hanged himself under a tree; the servant covered his body with leaves and fled.

sentences.zh: 事聞，上震悼，賜祭葬，諡果烈。

translations.literal: When word arrived the emperor was shaken and grieved, granted sacrificial funeral rites, and gave the posthumous title Guolie.
translations.idiomatic: When news reached the court the emperor was stricken with grief, granted state funeral honors, and gave him the posthumous title Guolie (Resolute and Fierce).

sentences.zh: 建旌勇祠京師，諸將死事者扎拉豐阿、觀音保、李全、王廷玉，命並祀，珠魯訥以自戕不與。

translations.literal: A Jingyong Shrine was built in the capital; the generals who died in service—Zhalafeng'a, Guanyinbao, Li Quan, and Wang Tingyu—were ordered to be worshipped together; Zhulune was excluded because he had killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: A Shrine of Martial Valor was built in the capital; the generals who died in service—Zhala Feng'a, Guanyinbao, Li Quan, and Wang Tingyu—were enshrined together, but Zhulune was excluded for having killed himself.

sentences.zh: 額爾登額及提督譚五格坐失機陷帥，逮詣京師，上廷鞫，用大逆律磔額爾登額，囚其父及女，並族屬戍新疆；

translations.literal: E'erdeng'e and Provincial Commander Tan Wuge were punished for missing their opportunity and causing the commander's ruin; they were arrested and brought to the capital. The emperor tried them at court, executed E'erdeng'e by dismemberment under the law of great treason, imprisoned his father and daughter, and exiled his clansmen to Xinjiang;
translations.idiomatic: E'erdeng'e and Provincial Commander Tan Wuge were held responsible for losing the moment and bringing disaster on their commander; both were arrested and brought to the capital. The emperor tried them in court, had E'erdeng'e dismembered under the law of great treason, imprisoned his father and daughter, and exiled his clan to Xinjiang;

sentences.zh: 譚五格亦棄市，而以其明日祭明瑞及扎拉豐阿、觀音保，上親臨奠。

translations.literal: Tan Wuge was also executed in the marketplace, and on the following day sacrifices were offered for Ming Rui, Zhalafeng'a, and Guanyinbao; the emperor personally attended the offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Wuge was also executed in public, and the next day the emperor personally offered sacrifices for Ming Rui, Zhala Feng'a, and Guanyinbao.

sentences.zh: 明瑞無子，以奎林子惠倫為嗣，襲爵。

translations.literal: Ming Rui had no son; Kuilin's son Huilun was made heir and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Rui had no son; Kuilin's son Huilun was adopted as heir and inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 自侍衛累遷奉宸院卿。

translations.literal: From imperial bodyguard he was promoted in succession to Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from imperial bodyguard to director of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，剿教匪湖北，自荊門、宜城逐賊入南漳山中，賜玉搬指、荷包；

translations.literal: Early in Jiaqing, suppressing sect bandits in Hubei, he drove the bandits from Jingmen and Yicheng into the mountains of Nanzhang and was bestowed a jade thumb ring and purse;
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiaqing reign, campaigning against sect rebels in Hubei, he drove them from Jingmen and Yicheng into the Nanzhang mountains and received a jade thumb ring and purse;

sentences.zh: 复逐賊至長坪，射賊渠，殪，餘賊兢集，中槍死，賜白金三千。

translations.literal: Again he pursued the bandits to Changping, shot the bandit leader dead; the remaining bandits gathered in alarm; he was hit by a musket ball and died; three thousand taels of silver were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: he pursued them again to Changping, shot the rebel leader dead, and as the rest swarmed in he was killed by musket fire; three thousand taels of silver were granted in reward.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：藻起詞科，以廉被主知，陟歷中外。

translations.literal: =Commentary= The commentary says: Zao rose through the erudition examination, was known to his sovereign for integrity, and ascended through central and provincial posts.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Zao rose through the special erudition examination, won the emperor's favor through integrity, and served both in the capital and in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 應琚持節臨邊，著聲績。

translations.literal: Yingju held the imperial commission on the frontier and achieved renown.
translations.idiomatic: Yingju held imperial commission on the frontier and built a distinguished record.

sentences.zh: 要皆不習軍旅，措注失條理，事敗身殉。

translations.literal: In sum, none were versed in military affairs; their arrangements lacked order, and when affairs failed they gave their lives.
translations.idiomatic: In the end none were trained in military affairs; their dispositions lacked order, and when events failed they died in the ruin.

sentences.zh: 明瑞深入，度敵不可勝，遣諸軍徐出，而躬自血戰，誓死不反顧，功雖不成，忠義凜烈，足以讋敵矣！

translations.literal: Ming Rui penetrated deeply, judged the enemy could not be overcome, sent the armies out slowly while he himself fought in bloody combat, vowing death and never turning back. Though merit was not achieved, his loyalty and righteousness were stern and fierce, enough to awe the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Ming Rui had penetrated too far, saw the enemy could not be beaten, sent the armies out while he fought on in person, swearing never to turn back. Though victory eluded him, his loyalty and courage were so fierce they could awe the foe!
